messages.content: You identify plain-language Discussion Units in a legal decision. Use only the supplied numbered paragraphs. Group contiguous paragraphs that perform one coherent task, such as procedural history, facts, party submissions, legal test, analysis/application, or disposition. Do not invent facts or citations. Return JSON with a units array. Each unit must contain start_paragraph, end_paragraph, label, explanation, transition_from_previous, and confidence. Use paragraph indices exactly as supplied; never output an index not present in the supplied list, and cover the supplied window from its first index through its last index exactly once. Keep explanations short and readable for a legal researcher.

{"case_id": 13881, "contract_version": "discussion_units_llm_v1", "deterministic_baseline": {"discussion_unit_count": 3, "units": [{"end_paragraph": 23, "generation_method": "discussion_unit_v1", "start_paragraph": 0}, {"end_paragraph": 25, "generation_method": "discussion_unit_v1", "start_paragraph": 24}, {"end_paragraph": 26, "generation_method": "discussion_unit_v1", "start_paragraph": 26}]}, "paragraph_window": {"first_allowed": 1, "last_allowed": 61}, "paragraphs": [{"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 1, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 1, "source_paragraph_index": 1, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[1] Mr. Osaj asks the Court to set aside the decision of the Appeal Division of the Social Security Tribunal [Appeal Division] denying him leave to appeal a decision of the General Division of that Tribunal [General Division]. At the General Division, Mr. Osaj succeeded in establishing his entitlement to a disability pension under the Canada Pension Plan, RSC 1985, c C-8 [CPP]. His application for leave to appeal did not challenge the granting of the pension, but its date of commencement. The General Division had found that he was disabled as of April 13, 2011, but he maintains that he was disabled 17 months earlier, when he was injured as the result of a workplace accident on November 27, 2009."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 2, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 2, "source_paragraph_index": 2, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[2] For the reasons that follow, this application must be allowed."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 3, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 3, "source_paragraph_index": 3, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[3] On November 27, 2009, Mr. Osaj sustained injuries as the result of a serious fall on a job site and he has not returned to work since then."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 4, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 4, "source_paragraph_index": 4, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[4] The General Division found that Mr. Osaj became disabled within the meaning of the CPP on April 13, 2011:"}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 8, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 5, "source_paragraph_index": 8, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[5] Mr. Osaj submitted that the General Division applied the wrong test when it found that his disability only became \u201csevere\u201d once he had reached \u201cmaximal medical recovery\u201d and had become \u201cpermanently disabled.\u201d He submitted there, as here, that these concepts form no part of the test for severity under paragraph 42(2)(a)(i) of the CPP, which instead requires that a disability render a person \u201cincapable regularly of pursuing any substantially gainful occupation.\u201d"}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 9, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 6, "source_paragraph_index": 9, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[6] The Appeal Division noted that the General Division had set out the correct test (at paragraphs 7, 9, 40, and 58 of its decision and not paragraphs 52 and 57 as the Appeal Division stated) and further found that when the General Division referred to the concepts of \u201cmaximal medical recovery\u201d and \u201cpermanent disability,\u201d it was not departing from the test for severity that it had previously articulated, but was quoting the language used in the medical reports upon which its determination of severity was made."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 10, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 7, "source_paragraph_index": 10, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[7] Mr. Osaj further submitted that the General Division had failed to provide adequate reasons for its selection of the date of onset of disability. In particular, he pointed out that there was other medical evidence, including an earlier report from Dr. Matthews, that spoke of him being disabled much earlier than April 2011."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 11, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 8, "source_paragraph_index": 11, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[8] The Appeal Division noted the General Division\u2019s statement that it had considered all of the medical reports before it. It held that the General Division was not unreasonable to identify April 13, 2011, as the date of onset of disability, based on Dr. Matthews\u2019 report of that date."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 12, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 9, "source_paragraph_index": 12, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[9] The only issue raised is whether it was reasonable for the Appeal Division to hold that Mr. Osaj had failed to raise a ground of appeal with a reasonable chance of success."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 13, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 10, "source_paragraph_index": 13, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[10] In large measure, Mr. Osaj challenges the Appeal Division\u2019s decision on the same grounds on which he challenged the General Division\u2019s decision. First, he submits that it was unreasonable for the Appeal Division to find that the General Division had applied the correct test for determining severity. Second, he submits that it was unreasonable for the Appeal Division to find that the General Division had given adequate reasons for selecting April 13, 2011, as the date of onset of his disability."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 14, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 11, "source_paragraph_index": 14, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[11] I agree with the Respondent that the test this Court must use when considering both issues is reasonableness: see Atkinson v Canada (Attorney General), 2014 FCA 187, [2015] 3 FCR 461 and Thibodeau c Canada (Procureur g\u00e9neral), 2015 CAF 167."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 15, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 12, "source_paragraph_index": 15, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[12] Subsection 58(1) of the Department of Employment and Social Development Act, SC 2005, c 34 sets out the permissible grounds of appeal from a decision of the General Division. It is not disputed that the grounds raised by Mr. Osaj fell within these accepted grounds. Leave is required to appeal a decision to the Appeal Division and subsection 58(2) of the Act provides that \u201cleave to appeal is refused if the Appeal Division is satisfied that the appeal has no reasonable chance of success.\u201d It is accepted that having a \u201creasonable chance of success\u201d in this context means having some arguable ground upon which the proposed appeal might succeed."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 16, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 13, "source_paragraph_index": 16, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[13] In my assessment, the two issues raised by Mr. Osaj are intertwined in that the General Division\u2019s decision that his disability commenced on April 13, 2011, may be said to be based on an improper test because the General Division fails to explain why, on the evidence before it, it picked that date and not an earlier one."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 17, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 14, "source_paragraph_index": 17, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[14] I agree with the Respondent that the General Division states the correct test for severe disability in its reasons, namely \u201cincapable [of] regularly pursuing any substantially gainful occupation.\u201d However, the Appeal Division fails to properly and reasonably address whether that was the test that the General Division actually used when it concluded that Mr. Osaj had a severe disability as at April 13, 2011."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 18, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 15, "source_paragraph_index": 18, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[15] The Appeal Division asserts that the General Division\u2019s choice of April 13, 2011, was based on the assessment by Dr. Matthews on that date, and that this choice was reasonable when read in the context of the other medical evidence. Frankly, I find that statement to be perverse."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 19, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 16, "source_paragraph_index": 19, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[16] The Appeal Division does address an earlier report from Dr. Mihic dated June 8, 2010, (on which the General Division stated it \u201cplaces weight \u2026 as it was forthright about the Appellant\u2019s medical condition and how it affects his capacity to work\u201d) in which he opined that \u201cthe applicant will not be able to return in the foreseen future to any kind of temporary and or permanent job.\u201d According to the Appeal Division, this report differs from the April 2011 report by Dr. Matthews because it is \u201cnot an unequivocal statement of disability.\u201d In my view, it is unreasonable to describe as equivocal a medical opinion that states that the patient is unable to work, even on a temporary basis, but leaves open the possibility of recovery at some point beyond the foreseeable future. The Appeal Division fails to explain why Dr. Mihic\u2019s opinion is not an opinion of severe disability nor does it explain why it saw it as equivocal when, on its face, it appears not to be."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 20, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 17, "source_paragraph_index": 20, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[17] The Appeal Division views a statement that Mr. Osaj had reached \u201cmaximal recovery\u201d and was \u201cpermanently disabled\u201d as an unequivocal statement of disability, even though neither term is the test for a severe disability. However, the Appeal Division fails to address how it can be said that the April 2011 report of Dr. Matthews is unequivocal but not his earlier report of February 1, 2011, in which he says that \u201cOsaj Xhemail has now permanent and serious impairment of all physical capabilities,\u201d \u201c[h]e has reached maximal medical recovery,\u201d \u201c[h]e is permanently disabled from work or looking for work,\u201d \u201c[h]is prognosis remains poor,\u201d and \u201c[h]e will remain disabled permanently.\u201d While Dr. Matthews\u2019 two reports are not identical, the language in both strikes me as equally forceful and I therefore can see no reason for concluding that only the latter report represents an \u201cunequivocal statement of disability.\u201d"}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 21, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 18, "source_paragraph_index": 21, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[18] Lastly, neither the General Division nor the Appeal Division address the following statement in Dr. Matthews\u2019 report dated June 2, 2011: \u201cMr. Osaj has a permanent disability with a very poor prognosis. All of the above are as of June 16 2010\u201d [emphasis added]. I cannot but note that the date of June 2010 coincides with the date of Dr. Mihic\u2019s report which the Appeal Division found to be equivocal."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 22, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 19, "source_paragraph_index": 22, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[19] I short, I find the decision of the Appeal Division to be unreasonable because it failed to adequately and carefully consider whether it was arguable that the General Division erred or made an unreasonable finding as to the onset date of Mr. Osaj\u2019s disability, in light of the record before it and the proper test to be applied."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 23, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 20, "source_paragraph_index": 23, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[20] Neither party sought costs. None are ordered."}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 5, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 57, "source_paragraph_index": 5, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[57] After considering all the evidence, the Tribunal finds it more likely than not that the Appellant had a severe and prolonged disability in April 2011 which is before his [Maximum Qualifying Period] of December 31, 2011. The Tribunal makes this finding particularly in light of the assessment of Dr. Matthews who reported on April 13, 2011, that the Appellant had reached maximal medical recovery and was \u201cpermanently disabled.\u201d"}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 6, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 58, "source_paragraph_index": 6, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[58] In short the Tribunal finds that on a balance of probabilities the Appellant was incapable regularly of pursuing any substantially gainful occupation as of April 2011. The Tribunal makes this finding based on medical reports and assessments of Dr. Mihic, Dr. Matthews, and Dr. Bringleson. The Tribunal also makes this finding based on the Appellant\u2019s oral testimony about his disability which was consistent, forthright, and credible.\n\u2026"}, {"citation_ids": [], "container_paragraph_index": 7, "is_heading": false, "paragraph_index": 61, "source_paragraph_index": 7, "statute_ids": [], "tag_ids": [], "text": "[61] The Tribunal finds that the Appellant had a severe and prolonged disability in April 2011 when Dr. Matthews reported that the Appellant was \u201cpermanently disabled.\u201d According to section 69 of the CPP, payments start four months after the date of disability. Payments start as of August 2011."}], "request_id": "discussion-units-case-13881"}
